# dsh-review
English | 简体中文

> **Deprecated.** DSH 0.2.2 ships the **Code review and changes** tab in the right
> Sidebar (`@deep

seek-ai/dsh-experimental-client-ui-forge`): this session's code
> changes, per-file diffs, line comm

ents and change requests. That covers what
> this panel did, so the plugin is no longer needed and n

o longer maintained. The
> repository stays online for reference; it is only worth installing if you

are
> pinned to DSH 0.2.1 or earlier.

A **review-first Git panel for the DSH Web GUI**. It adds one tab to the right
Sidebar that answers

the questions a code review actually asks: what is dirty in my
work tree, what does this commit chan

ge, how does my branch compare to another one,
and which branch am I on — without a terminal and wit
hout touching history.

- **Working tree**: staged, unstaged, and untracked files, each with its `+/-` counts
- **Commits**:
the current branch's history, page by page, each row tagged with the refs pointing at it (`main`, `
origin/main`, tags); a commit opens its message, author, and changed files, and any file opens its d

iff
- **Branches**: local and remote branches tagged apart, each with its last commit; local branche
s show how many commits are not pushed yet, one click switches, and `对比` diffs a local branch agains

t its upstream (or against `HEAD` when it tracks nothing)
- **Sub-projects**: when the working direc
tory is a container rather than a repository, the panel lists the Git work trees below it and rememb

ers the choice per Session
- **Diffs** are real `git diff` output — renames, binary files, and mode

changes included — rendered line by line with the Host's own syntax highlighting
- **Read-only by de
sign**: no commit, no push, no stage, no reset. The only write is `git checkout`, and it refuses a d
irty work tree instead of stashing or forcing
## Screenshots
## Install
### 1. Through the Host's `installBundle` (installs **and** enables)
Ask the agent in a conversation:
> install the plugin `github:miiy/dsh-review`
or paste the same spec into the install field on **Settings → Plugins**.

Both call the Host's `installBundle`, which installs the package, adds it to
`dsh.profile.bundles`,
and hot-applies it — one step.
### 2. From the CLI (`dsh plugin`, installs only)
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`dsh plugin` forwards its arguments to pnpm inside the profile directory, so this
step installs the

package but does **not** compose it. The row then shows up on
**Settings → Plugins** as installed an

d switched **off**; turn it on to add it to
`dsh.profile.bundles`. If the switch does not take effec

t live, restart `dsh web`.
A plain-JavaScript bundle has no build script, so a git install needs no

`allowBuilds` approval. A local checkout works too:
`dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /path/to/dsh

lds` approval. A local checkout works too:
`dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /path/to/dsh-review`.
### 3. Start the Host

Then start `dsh web` as usual. No launch flag is needed: the bundle registers its
route on the Host'

s `webServer` when it mounts, and the tab shows up in the right
Sidebar's tab guide.
## Use

Open the right Sidebar and pick **Git 审查 / Git Review** from the tab guide (`+`).
The panel follows

the Session's working directory, so each conversation reviews its
own repository.
| Tab | What it shows |

| Changes | Staged, unstaged, and untracked files; click a file for its diff |
| Commits | History o

f the checked-out branch; click a commit for its files, then a file for its diff |
| Branches | Loca
l branches with `↑` unpushed commits (and `↓` behind), then remote branches; **Switch** asks for an
inline confirmation, **Compare** diffs a local branch against its upstream (or against `HEAD` when i
t tracks nothing) and lists the changed files, each opening its diff |

`Refresh` re-reads whatever the panel is showing. Switching away and back also
refreshes, and nothin
g polls in the background.

Click the repository name in the header to switch between the Git work trees the
Session can reach:

the one containing the working directory, plus any nested one
down to four levels. A Session directo

ry that is not itself a repository picks its
only candidate automatically, and asks when there are s

is not itself a repository picks its
only candidate automatically, and asks when there are several.
## Safety
- Every git command runs through `spawn('git', [...])` with an argument list — never a shell string.
- References are fenced by `rev-parse --verify`, paths must be repository-relative (no `..`, no lea

ding dash).
- Commands carry `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`; diffs use `--no-col

or --no-ext-diff --no-textconv`.
- `checkout` refuses any staged or unstaged tracked change and retu

rns the affected files. Untracked files alone do not block it.
- The route is fenced with the Host c
onnection's `requestRejection`, so a non-loopback request without a same-origin or paired origin is

rejected.
- A repository the client asks for must be the work tree the Session directory sits in, or
one inside it; anything else answers `forbidden-root`.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.2.1-rc.1 < 0.3.0` on the Web profile
- `git` on the Host, and the Session w
orking directory inside a git working tree
## Limitations
- One repository at a time: the one containing the working directory, or a nested one the panel offe

rs.
- No commit, push, stage/unstage, stash, or history rewrite.
- Syntax highlighting is off when t

he Host does not export `useCodeHighlighter`; rows still render as plain text.
- A working directory
outside a repository, or a Host without `git`, answers `not-a-repository` and the panel says so.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`test/` needs no dependency; the `node_modules/@deepseek-ai/schemastery` link the
route tests use on
ly mirrors what the profile provides at runtime.
| File | Role |

| `git.js` | git execution, output parsers, reference and path fencing |
| `index.js` | Host plugin:

the `/dsh-review/api/<method>` route |
| `client.js` | Client bundle: the Sidebar tab type and its

body |
| `MAINTENANCE.md` | every upstream name this plugin depends on |
